categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Full SSR on all pages — content in initial HTML, no JavaScript rendering dependency

Sitemap: 94 URLs, all 200 OK, all with accurate lastmod, declared in robots.txt
Canonical tags present on all content pages
Redirect chains: HTTP to HTTPS in one hop, www to non-www in one hop, no multi-hop chains
TTFB: 60-83ms (Vercel CDN HIT on all audited pages)
AI crawlers explicitly named in robots.txt with Allow: /
llms.txt: present, complete (35/35 blog posts indexed), 15+ FAQ pairs, RSL 1.0 licensed

findings.title: og:image missing on all 12 service pages
findings.description: Every service page defines its own openGraph metadata block without an images key. Next.js App Router replaces (not merges) the root layout openGraph, stripping the og-default.png fallback. All 12 service pages render text-only social cards. Confirmed missing via source code review and live HTTP header inspection.
findings.recommendation: Add images: [{ url: 'https://suitepacific.com/og-default.png', width: 1200, height: 630 }] to every service page openGraph block. Consider extracting a shared defaultOpenGraph constant in lib/seo.ts to prevent future recurrence.

findings.title: /suitecompare marketing page missing canonical and og:image
findings.description: The /suitecompare product landing page is correctly indexed (robots: index, follow override in page.tsx) and in the sitemap, but lacks an alternates.canonical self-reference and an og:image.
findings.recommendation: Add alternates: { canonical: 'https://suitepacific.com/suitecompare' } and openGraph images to app/suitecompare/page.tsx metadata.

findings.title: No IndexNow implementation
findings.description: No IndexNow key file found. With 6-12 new posts per month, Bing indexing relies entirely on crawl discovery. IndexNow primarily benefits Bing Copilot citation freshness.
findings.recommendation: Generate a UUID key, place it at /public/[key].txt, ping api.indexnow.org on each deploy or publish event.

findings.title: CSP frame-ancestors 'none' conflicts with X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
findings.description: Two headers express contradictory framing policies. Modern browsers follow CSP; XFO is redundant and inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Align both headers: either frame-ancestors 'none' + X-Frame-Options: DENY, or frame-ancestors 'self' + X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN.

findings.title: CSP script-src contains unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval
findings.description: These directives negate XSS protection. Next.js 15 App Router supports nonce-based CSP to eliminate both.
findings.recommendation: Implement nonce-based CSP via Next.js middleware.

findings.title: X-XSS-Protection header is deprecated
findings.description: X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block is not recognized by modern browsers and can cause regressions on legacy environments.
findings.recommendation: Set X-XSS-Protection: 0 per OWASP. A properly scoped CSP replaces its function.

findings.title: Case study sitemap lastmod values all share one date
findings.description: All 6 case studies carry lastmod: 2026-06-01 (a batch date, not individual modification dates). Google uses lastmod for re-crawl scheduling.
findings.recommendation: Derive sitemap lastmod from each case study's actual publication date field.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Technical accuracy is high throughout — NetSuite-specific nuances are correct
39 blog posts and 30 resource pages covering practitioner-level topics
Quick Answer boxes on 12 posts (134-167 word self-contained answers)
FAQ sections on 12 posts with structured Q&A format
All posts under 3 months old — within the AI freshness citation window
LeadFormLight placed before content and at the bottom on all blog/resource pages

findings.title: Two blog posts still under 900 prose words
findings.description: netsuite-payment-runs-2026-2 (~882 words) and netsuite-bank-reconciliation-changes-2026-2 (~923 words) are the only remaining thin posts. These are 2026.2 release posts that were expanded in the prior round but didn't reach 1000 words.
findings.recommendation: Expand both posts to 1000+ prose words by adding a before/after configuration scenario, common edge cases, and an FAQ section.

findings.title: 5 blog posts with zero internal links
findings.description: netsuite-payment-adjustments-2026-2, netsuite-payment-runs-2026-2, netsuite-rest-batch-sequential, netsuite-sales-order-fulfillment-list, and signs-netsuite-support-not-working have no internal links. The signs post is the most critical gap: high commercial-intent with no link to /netsuite-post-go-live-support.
findings.recommendation: Add at minimum one service page link and one related post link per zero-link post.

findings.title: Opening paragraphs bury the direct answer
findings.description: High-intent posts open with narrative hooks rather than direct answers. AI systems extract the first 1-2 sentences of a passage for citations. Posts affected: netsuite-saved-search-tips, netsuite-workflow-vs-suitescript, signs-netsuite-support-not-working, netsuite-month-end-close-checklist, workflow-automation-mistakes.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the first paragraph of these 5 posts to deliver the direct answer before framing.

findings.title: 11 blog/resource near-duplicate pairs may split topical authority
findings.description: Eleven blog/resource pairs cover the same NetSuite topic (blog: what changed; resource: how to do it). Individual pages range from 450-900 prose words. Where content overlaps more than 70%, consider consolidating or adding canonical.
findings.recommendation: Verify each pair has genuinely distinct intent. Where overlap exceeds 70%, consolidate or ensure each piece stands alone at 700+ prose words.

findings.title: Oracle certifications invisible in visible content
findings.description: Certifications are in the OrganizationJsonLd award array and one hire page card title, not in visible prose on primary service pages. Google quality raters look for verifiable credentials in visible content.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief credential callout to the hero section of /netsuite-post-go-live-support and /netsuite-suitescript-development.

findings.title: FSM cluster has no hub linking all four posts together
findings.description: Four FSM posts cover the August 2026 bundle update with no page linking to all four. Individual posts link to /contact only — zero link equity flows to any service page.
findings.recommendation: Create a short FSM pillar post, or link all four posts to /netsuite-administrator-support as an interim solution.

findings.title: No CFO/Controller-targeted content
findings.description: All 69 content pages target NetSuite admins and developers. CFO and Controller personas are not addressed.
findings.recommendation: Add 2-3 posts per quarter targeting finance-leader search intent. Lead with business outcome framing.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Title tags present on all pages
Meta descriptions present on all pages
H1 tags present on all pages
Blog posts have descriptive, keyword-rich titles

findings.title: Homepage title cannibalizes /netsuite-post-go-live-support
findings.description: Homepage title 'SuitePacific: Post-Go-Live NetSuite Support & Optimization' directly targets the same keyword cluster as the dedicated service page. The homepage likely outranks the dedicated page, sending commercial traffic to the wrong destination.
findings.recommendation: Revise homepage title to a brand-hub statement. Give /netsuite-post-go-live-support full keyword ownership.

findings.title: Meta descriptions over 160 characters on service pages
findings.description: Service page meta descriptions range 182-202 characters. Google truncates at ~160 characters, reducing CTR from the truncation point.
findings.recommendation: Trim service page meta descriptions to 150-160 characters. Front-load the primary benefit.

findings.title: Blog posts lack H3 sub-headings for granular passage indexing
findings.description: All posts use only H2 headings. Posts over 1,500 words covering 3+ subtopics per H2 would benefit from H3 sub-sections for passage-level indexing.
findings.recommendation: Add H3 headings to posts over 1,500 words. Priority: netsuite-workflow-vs-suitescript, netsuite-map-reduce-script-guide, netsuite-saved-search-examples.

findings.title: Blog post titles over 60 characters (SERP truncation)
findings.description: All checked blog post titles exceed 60 characters (70-92 range) due to '| SuitePacific' suffix. Google truncates at ~60 characters in most SERPs.
findings.recommendation: Where title + ' | SuitePacific' exceeds 65 characters, shorten the title itself. Low priority — cosmetic, not a ranking factor.

ProfessionalService + WebSite + FAQPage on homepage

findings.title: Resource TechArticle schema image: logo-icon.png (256x256) declared as 1200x630
findings.description: app/(site)/resources/[slug]/page.tsx line 63 sets the TechArticle image to logo-icon.png with width: 1200, height: 630. The actual file is 256x256. Google validates image dimensions for Article rich results; a 256px-wide image fails the 1200px minimum and blocks all 30 resource pages from image-enhanced rich results.
findings.recommendation: Change image URL to og-default.png (confirmed 1200x630) in app/(site)/resources/[slug]/page.tsx line 63.

findings.title: Article/TechArticle/BlogPosting missing url property
findings.description: mainEntityOfPage provides the WebPage @id, but article entities should also carry a url property. Affects BlogPostingJsonLd (components/seo/JsonLd.tsx), case study Article, and TechArticle in resources/[slug]/page.tsx.
findings.recommendation: Add url: absolute-canonical-url to each article block. Three one-line additions.

findings.title: Publisher logo ImageObject missing width and height
findings.description: The publisher.logo ImageObject in BlogPosting, Article, and TechArticle blocks declares url: logo-icon.png with no width or height. Actual dimensions are 256x256.
findings.recommendation: Add width: 256, height: 256 to all three publisher logo declarations.

findings.title: /netsuite-implementation-partner-vs-managed-support missing Article schema
findings.description: This long-form comparison guide has only BreadcrumbList and FAQPage. No Article schema means it is ineligible for Article rich results.
findings.recommendation: Add an inline Article block using og-default.png as the image.

findings.title: Blog and Resources index pages missing collection schema
findings.description: /blog has only BreadcrumbList. /resources has only BreadcrumbList.
findings.recommendation: Add Blog schema to /blog and CollectionPage schema to /resources.

findings.title: ProfessionalService missing @id anchor
findings.description: OrganizationJsonLd has no @id, so service pages cannot reference the organization entity by ID. Limits Google's entity graph connection.
findings.recommendation: Add '@id': 'https://suitepacific.com/#organization' to OrganizationJsonLd.

findings.title: FAQPage no longer produces Google rich results (info only)
findings.description: Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites on May 7, 2026. FAQPage blocks are harmless but produce no SERP feature.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. Do not remove existing blocks.

findings.description: The homepage HTML references 13 JS chunk files loaded async. This is standard for Next.js App Router code splitting. No blocking scripts detected.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: AI crawlers explicitly allowed: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot all have named User-Agent blocks with Allow: /
Full SSR — content accessible without JavaScript to all AI crawlers
llms.txt: present, complete (35/35 blog posts indexed), 15+ FAQ pairs, RSL 1.0 licensed
Quick Answer boxes on 12 posts (134-167 words, self-contained)
All 35 posts under 3 months old — within the 3x AI citation boost window

findings.title: Zero question-based H2 headings across all 35 posts
findings.description: All posts use declarative H2s. AI systems match section headings against user queries. Question headings ('When should you use a Client Script?') match directly; declarative headings ('What a Client Script actually is') require the AI to infer intent.
findings.recommendation: Rephrase H2s on 5 priority posts to question format: netsuite-workflow-vs-suitescript, netsuite-map-reduce-script-guide, netsuite-user-event-vs-client-script, suitescript-best-practices, netsuite-post-go-live-checklist.

findings.title: Blog post openers too short for AI citation (40-85 words vs 134-167 optimal)
findings.description: ~44% of AI citations come from the first 30% of a page. Current openers are narrative hooks, not answer blocks. Posts without Quick Answer boxes have no self-contained citable passage near the top.
findings.recommendation: For the 23 posts without Quick Answer boxes, add a 130-160 word Quick Summary block immediately after the first paragraph.

findings.title: SVG diagram content not accessible to AI crawlers
findings.description: Technical posts embed inline SVGs with text elements. AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) do not parse SVG text. Every insight locked inside an SVG is uncitable. Approximately 10-15 diagrams affected.
findings.recommendation: Add a plain-text figcaption after each SVG diagram stating the key conclusion in 1-2 sentences.

findings.title: No Reddit or YouTube brand presence
findings.description: YouTube mentions correlate 0.737 with AI citation rates (Ahrefs 75K-brand study, strongest single off-site signal). Reddit correlates at 0.46+. Both are absent.
findings.recommendation: Start with r/NetSuite (~45,000 members): answer 2-3 SuiteScript/workflow questions per week using genuine expertise.
